title: LED：为什么一定要限流电阻
summary: 先不加电阻，让 LED 烧一次（反正是仿真）。再算出该用多大的电阻。
concepts: forward voltage Vf 正向压降
description: LED 两端的电压几乎固定（正向压降 Vf），电源多出来的电压必须由一个串联电阻吃掉，否则电流会大到烧坏 LED。本课先把 LED 直接接在 5 V 上看它“烧掉”，再按 R = (Vs − Vf) / I 选电阻重搭。

cards.title: 不加电阻，直接接
text: 在真实世界里这一步会烧掉一颗 LED。这里是仿真，**放心烧**。
把 LED 直接接在 5 V 和 GND 之间，什么都不串，然后看右边的**诊断**。

cards.title: LED 是一道矮水坝
text: - LED 导通以后，两端电压几乎**固定**在它的正向压降 $V_f$：红 ≈ 1.8 V，黄 ≈ 2.0 V，**绿 ≈ 2.1 V**，蓝 / 白 ≈ 3.0 V。
![](fig:iv)
- 电源有 5 V，LED 只“拦住”2.1 V。剩下的 2.9 V 没人拦，就全压在 LED 内部很小的电阻上——电流冲得很大，LED 烧了。
- 解决办法：**串一个电阻，让它替 LED 吃掉多出来的电压。** 串联时电流处处相同，所以：
$$R = \frac{V_s - V_f}{I}$$
![](fig:budget)

cards.title: 加上电阻，重新搭
text: 拔掉烧掉的 LED，在 +5 V 和 LED 之间串一个 150 Ω。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **长脚是正极**（接 + 那边），短脚（灯头上有一个小平面的那边）是负极。插反了不亮。
- 5 V 下插反一般不会坏；但常见 LED 只能承受约 5 V 的**反向**电压，9 V、12 V 电路里插反就可能击穿。
- 一般 LED **5–20 mA** 就够亮，不要超过 25 mA。电阻放在 LED 前面还是后面都行：串联电路里电流处处相同。
- 粗算和实测差一点很正常：LED 的电压会随电流略微升高（本模拟器把它当成 $V_f$ 再加一个约 12 Ω 的小电阻）。

caption.text: LED 像一道矮水坝：电压不到 V_f 几乎没有电流；一过 V_f，电压只多一点点，电流就猛涨。

i18n.en: An LED is a low dam: below V_f almost no current flows; past V_f a tiny bit more voltage sends the current soaring.

caption.text: 5 V 分成两份：LED 拦住 V_f，剩下的 V_R 全落在电阻上，电阻值决定电流。

i18n.en: The 5 V splits in two: the LED holds back V_f, the rest, V_R, falls across the resistor, and the resistor sets the current.

en.title: LEDs: why the resistor is not optional
en.summary: First let an LED burn out with no resistor (it's a simulation). Then work out the resistor it needs.
en.description: An LED holds an almost fixed voltage (its forward voltage Vf); the rest of the supply voltage has to be dropped by a series resistor, or the current gets big enough to destroy the LED. In this lesson you first wire an LED straight across 5 V and watch it burn, then pick the resistor with R = (Vs − Vf) / I and rebuild.
hints: LED dark? First check its direction: long lead to the resistor (the + side), short lead to GND.
R = (V − Vf) / I. A green LED has Vf ≈ 2.1 V.
tests: LED on, sensible voltage across the resistor

cards.title: Straight across, no resistor
text: In the real world this step costs you an LED. Here it's a simulation — **go ahead and burn it**.
Put an LED straight between 5 V and GND with nothing in series, then watch the **diagnostics** on the right.

cards.title: An LED is a low dam
text: - Once an LED conducts, the voltage across it stays almost **fixed** at its forward voltage $V_f$: red ≈ 1.8 V, yellow ≈ 2.0 V, **green ≈ 2.1 V**, blue / white ≈ 3.0 V.
![](fig:iv)
- The supply has 5 V and the LED only "holds back" 2.1 V. The other 2.9 V has nothing to stop it, so it all lands on the tiny resistance inside the LED — a huge current, and the LED is gone.
- The fix: **put a resistor in series and let it take the extra voltage.** In series the current is the same everywhere, so:
$$R = \frac{V_s - V_f}{I}$$
![](fig:budget)
For about 20 mA: $R = \frac{5 - 2.1}{0.02} = 145$ Ω; take the nearest standard value, **150 Ω**.

cards.title: Add the resistor and rebuild
text: Remove the burned LED and put 150 Ω in series between +5 V and the LED.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **The long lead is the anode** (towards +); the short lead, on the side where the LED body has a small flat, is the cathode. Reversed, it stays dark.
- At 5 V a reversed LED usually survives; but common LEDs only take about 5 V in **reverse**, so in a 9 V or 12 V circuit a reversed LED can break down.
- **5–20 mA** is bright enough for most LEDs; stay under 25 mA. The resistor can go before or after the LED: in series the current is the same everywhere.
- A small gap between the estimate and the reading is normal: an LED's voltage rises a little with current (this simulator models it as $V_f$ plus a small resistance of about 12 Ω).

steps: Pick **Breadboard power module** and click **`tp1`** (keep **5 V**): its four pins go into tp1, tn1, bp1 and bn1, so both pairs of rails are powered.
Two **jumpers**: red **`tp4`** → **`a4`**, blue **`a11`** → **`tn11`**. Column 4 is +5 V and column 11 is GND.
**Green LED**: long lead in **`c4`**, short lead in **`c11`** — straight across 5 V and GND. Look at the **diagnostics**: how big is the current? What happened to the LED?
**Resistor** in **`b4`**–**`b8`**, set to **`150 Ω`** in **Properties**. A resistor has no polarity; either lead can go first.
A new **green LED**: long lead in **`c8`** (to the resistor), short lead in **`c11`** (to GND). The long lead faces the + side!
The LED is lit and the diagnostics are quiet. Press **Check my circuit**, then **click the LED**: Properties on the right show the current through it.

measurements.ask: Predict first, then look: click the LED — what current do Properties show?
measurements.explain: Rough estimate: (5 − 2.1) / 150 ≈ 19 mA; counting the LED's own 12 Ω, (5 − 2.1) / (150 + 12) ≈ 17.9 mA. About 1 mA apart — the rough estimate is good enough for picking a resistor.

measurements.ask: Swap the 150 Ω for 330 Ω. The LED will be:
choices: Dimmer: a bigger resistor leaves roughly half the current
The same: the LED voltage is fixed
measurements.explain: The resistor still takes about 2.9 V; with more than twice the resistance the current drops to under half — dimmer, but still lit.

measurements.ask: What happens if you plug the LED in backwards in this 5 V circuit?
choices: It stays dark and is usually fine
measurements.explain: An LED only lets current flow from the long lead to the short one. Reversed, almost no current flows, and 5 V doesn't exceed a common LED's reverse rating of about 5 V.

tests.name: LED 亮，电阻上的电压合理

measurements.ask: 先预测，再看：选中 LED，「属性」里显示的电流是多少？
measurements.explain: 粗算 (5 − 2.1) / 150 ≈ 19 mA；把 LED 里那 12 Ω 也算进去，(5 − 2.1) / (150 + 12) ≈ 17.9 mA。差 1 mA 左右，挑电阻时用粗算就够了。

measurements.ask: 把 150 Ω 换成 330 Ω，LED 会？
choices: 更暗：电阻大了，电流大约只剩一半
不变：LED 的电压是固定的
measurements.explain: 电阻上的电压还是约 2.9 V，电阻变成两倍多，电流就变成不到一半，LED 变暗，但仍然亮。

measurements.ask: 如果在这个 5 V 电路里把 LED 插反，会怎样？
measurements.explain: LED 只让电流从长脚流向短脚。反向时几乎没有电流；5 V 也还没有超过常见 LED 约 5 V 的反向耐压。

steps.text: 选**「面包板电源模块」**，单击 **`tp1`**（保持 **5 V**）：它的四根针同时插进 tp1、tn1、bp1、bn1，上下两组轨道都有电了。
**绿色 LED**：长脚插 **`c4`**，短脚插 **`c11`**——直接跨在 5 V 和 GND 之间。看**诊断**：电流有多大？LED 怎么了？
选中这颗 LED，按 **Delete** 删掉。
新的**绿色 LED**：长脚插 **`c8`**（接电阻），短脚插 **`c11`**（接 GND）。长脚要朝向 + 那一侧！
LED 亮了，诊断也不报警了。点**「检查我的电路」**，然后**单击选中 LED**：右边「属性」里会显示流过它的电流。

hints: LED 不亮？先看是不是插反了：长脚接电阻（+ 那侧），短脚接 GND。
R = (V − Vf) / I。绿色 LED 的 Vf 约 2.1 V。
